The prize is open to entrants from all across Australia over the age of 16. Mosman council funds the prize and acquires each year’s winning artwork, forming the basis of the Mosman Art Collection. Now in its 79th year the Mosman Art Prize has provided a historical timeline of contemporary painting practice in Australia. Mosman Art Prize Established in 1947, the Mosman Art Prize is Australia’s oldest local government art award. It was founded by the artist, architect and arts advocate, Alderman Allan Gamble, at a time when only a small handful of art prizes were in existence in Australia and the community had very little support and few opportunities to exhibit their work. Find out more The 2026 Mosman Art Prize entries are now open. Find out more. Mosman Art Gallery acknowledges the Borogegal and Cammeraigal people as the traditional custodians of this land. It was initiated in 1988 by the internationally renowned artist and local resident Ken Done AM. The Prize is open to all young people aged 12-21 years and is one of the richest youth art prizes in Australia. Online entries are now open for the 2024 Youth Art Prize – find out more . Projects in this stream must have a clear pathway towards a future public presentation for Australian audiences. They may also seek to reach international audiences. Applicants should show how they will develop the partnerships, resources and investment needed to support that future outcome. The aim of Development investment is to help works reach proof-of-concept stage and enable them to secure further investment, co-producing partners and presenting partners. Please note that the Creative Futures Fund is not designed to support early-stage creative development of a new and untested idea. Projects in early-stage development may be more suitable for other funding opportunities.
